A.explanation: Flavour is a descriptive sensation, not a quantity that can be expressed as a magnitude with a unit.

B.explanation: Kelvin, symbol $\text{K}$, is the SI unit of temperature, not the physical quantity itself.

C.explanation: Minute is a unit of the quantity time, equal to $60 \text{ s}$, not a physical quantity itself.

D.explanation: Potential difference is a physical quantity that has a magnitude and is measured in volts $\text{V}$.

hints: Notice the question asks for a physical quantity, which must have a numerical value that can be measured and expressed with a unit.
Check whether kelvin and minute are things you measure or the units you measure in for temperature and time.
Check which of flavour and potential difference can be given a value in a unit such as $\text{V}$.
walkthrough: Recall the definition: a physical quantity can be measured and is expressed as a numerical magnitude followed by a unit, for example $5.0 \text{ V}$.
Flavour cannot be expressed in this way because it is a qualitative description with no measuring unit.
Kelvin is the SI base unit for the quantity thermodynamic temperature, and minute is a unit for the quantity time, so neither is a quantity.
Potential difference can be measured with a voltmeter and expressed with a magnitude and the unit volt, for example $12 \text{ V}$, so it satisfies the definition. This is option D.
